profile.reading:
Flexential is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and formed from the 2017 merger of two predecessor colocation companies, Peak 10, founded in 2000 to serve the Southeastern US, and ViaWest, founded in 1999 to serve the Western US. The combined company took the Flexential name in 2018 after also acquiring AppliedTrust and INetU in 2015 to expand its professional services and cloud portfolio.

The company is privately held, GI Partners is its controlling sponsor per Flexentials own announcement of a GI Partners continuation vehicle and a GI Data Infrastructure strategic investment, and North Carolina business press separately reports Flexential received a strategic investment from a Morgan Stanley infrastructure unit. Flexentials site states the company secured $2.1 billion in financing in 2021 for growth and sustainability initiatives, and describes its footprint only in round terms, more than 40 data centers across 18 national markets, with more than 800 employees and 3,000 customers across more than 20 industries, without a precise facility count, megawatt capacity figure, or per-market investment breakdown.

The registry here tracks 43 Flexential facilities across fifteen states, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Minnesota, North Carolina, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia, a wide multi-region colocation footprint consistent with the ViaWest and Peak 10 predecessor geographies it was built from, Western states from ViaWest, Southeastern states from Peak 10. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Flexential Brentwood Data Center in Williamson County, TN, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to Flexential based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
Flexential Brentwood Data Center in Williamson County, Tennessee, publishes 1.49 MW of IT capacity across 19,150 square feet of technical space, operated by .

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 149 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 37 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Brentwood Data Center holds 7 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Tennessee has 5 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 12.13 MW. Flexential Brentwood Data Center contributes 1.49 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
